newsitem.title: FRANCE: Essilor sees net debt stable at end 96.
newsitem.headline: Essilor sees net debt stable at end 96.

text.p: The net debt of French eye glass and contact lense maker Essilor should remain steady at two billion francs at the end of 1996, unchanged from its level at the end of the first half, the company's communications director, Nicole Micheletti, said on Thursday.

She told an investment seminar organised by Bourse Ferri that the debt-to-equity ratio which was around 54 percent at the end of June 1996 should be slightly lower by the end of the year. She reiterated the group's aim was to cut the debt to equity ratio to 40 percent.

At end 1995, Essilor's net debt of 711 million francs represented 20 percent of shareholders equity and Essilor had cash flow of 827 million francs. But it bought four North American laboratories this year for 1.3 billion francs.
Micheletti said Essilor had no plans for further North American purchases and had made Europe its "major priority".

She would not comment on statements by Jean-Louis Beffa, chairman of Saint-Gobain, who did not rule out increasing the glassmaker's stake in Essilor. Saint-Gobain holds 27 percent of the voting rights of Essilor.
